newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end firm on pre-budget confidence.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end firm on pre-budget confidence.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed firmer on Tuesday, driven mainly by small retailers' optimism about Wednesday's budget and the pre-arranged sale of a large parcel of a blue-chip counter, brokers said.
They said a crossing of 82,000 shares of conglomerate John Keells at 185 rupees, which was up by four rupees, helped push up the all-share index by 2.1 points to close at 617.3.
Turnover was 31.8 million rupees, down from Monday's 43.6 million. Foreign purchases were 17.7 million rupees while foreign sales totalled 16.6 million rupees. Gains outnumbered losses 24 to nine.
"Except for the crossing, the market was retail-driven," said Hussain Gani, an investment advisor at John Keells Stock Brokers, a subsidiary of the holding group of the same name.
Retailers, anticipating a market-friendly 1997 state budget, have been pushing the market up with consistent buying of small volumes, Gani said.
Agalawatte Plantations was up 5.75 to 33.25. Tea Smallholder Factories was up 1.75 to 28 rupees. Richard Pieris Exports fell 2.50 to 21 rupees.
